cards.explanation: The answer is the whole congregation. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “…assemble the whole congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” (Leviticus 8:3) Not a few reps, not a small committee. Everybody. I get nervous when two people watch me stamp one cookie, so I think Aaron, the man being ordained, had a big day ahead.

The answer is False. Moses doesn't ask for more days. The text says, “So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” (Leviticus 8:4) Moses, Israel's leader, does what he was told, and the assembly gathers. I'd have needed a reminder alarm and a sticky note, friends.

The answer is water. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…presented Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.” (Leviticus 8:6) Clean comes first, and the fancy clothes come after. Even my cookie sheets get a wash before the next batch.

The answer is a gold plate called the holy diadem. Moses, Israel's leader, “…set the gold plate, the holy diadem, on the front of the turban, as the LORD had commanded him.” (Leviticus 8:9) The turban goes on Aaron's head, and the gold plate goes right on the front. Nobody has to wonder where to look.

The answer is seven. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times…” (Leviticus 8:11) He anoints the altar, its utensils, and the basin with its stand. Seven rounds with the oil, friends, and that's a very thorough job.

The answer is True. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.” (Leviticus 8:12) First the tabernacle and the altar get the oil. Then Aaron himself does, right on his head. It's the man too, not only the things.

The answer is tunics and sashes and headbands. Moses, Israel's leader, “…put tunics on them, wrapped sashes around them, and tied headbands on them, just as the LORD had commanded him.” (Leviticus 8:13) The sons get a simpler outfit than Aaron's. I can tell you right now my apron has more steps than I'd like, so simpler sounds nice.

The answer is hands. After Moses, Israel's leader, brought the bull near for the sin offering, “…Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.” (Leviticus 8:14) Hands are the one tool nobody has to dig for. I spent years in a junk drawer and never once lost mine.

The answer is to purify and consecrate it. Moses, Israel's leader, put the blood on the four horns of the altar, “…purifying the altar.” Then he “…consecrated it so that atonement could be made on it.” (Leviticus 8:15) The text spells out the purpose, so there's no guessing. The blood goes on the altar to get it ready.

The answer is that he burns it outside the camp. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “burned” the bull with its hide, flesh and dung “…outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded him.” (Leviticus 8:17) The fat went on the altar, and the rest went outside. Outside the camp, as commanded.

The answer is on all sides of the altar. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, slaughtered the ram “…and splattered the blood on all sides of the altar.” (Leviticus 8:19) Every side, and no side gets skipped. That's the burnt offering ram, the first of the two.

The answer is that he washes them and burns them too. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…washed the entrails and legs with water and burned the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering…” (Leviticus 8:21) Washed first, then burned with the rest. The whole ram goes up, with nothing left behind.

The answer is his right earlobe, right thumb and right big toe. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, put some of the blood “…on Aaron’s right earlobe, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.” (Leviticus 8:23) That's three spots, and all of them are on the right side. It's ear to toe, and the list is very specific.

The answer is False. The sons get the blood too. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…presented Aaron’s sons and put some of the blood on their right earlobes, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet.” (Leviticus 8:24) It's the same three spots as Aaron's, so nobody gets left out.

The answer is that it's waved before the LORD. Moses, Israel's leader, put it all in their hands “…and waved them before the LORD as a wave offering.” (Leviticus 8:27) Then Moses took it from their hands and burned it on the altar with the burnt offering. Fat, a thigh and bread, all in one load, with the assembly gathered. I can't carry one tray of cookies to the counter without leaving a crumb trail, so I'm impressed.

The answer is False. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, took these from their hands and “…burned them on the altar with the burnt offering.” (Leviticus 8:28) It's called “…an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.” So Aaron and his sons hand it over, and they don't keep it.

The answer is garments. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, sprinkled the oil and the blood on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. “So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, as well as Aaron’s sons and their garments.” (Leviticus 8:30) The clothes are named right alongside the men. Garments shows up four times in that one verse, so it's hard to miss, friends.

The answer is True. Moses, Israel's leader, tells Aaron and his sons, “Then you must burn up the remainder of the meat and bread.” (Leviticus 8:32) They boil the meat and eat it at the entrance first. Whatever is left over goes into the fire.

The answer is atonement. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “What has been done today has been commanded by the LORD in order to make atonement on your behalf.” (Leviticus 8:34) The LORD commanded it, and atonement is the reason Moses gives. It isn't just a ceremony for show.

The answer is so that they will not die. Moses, Israel's leader, tells Aaron and his sons, “You must remain at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD’s charge so that you will not die…” (Leviticus 8:35) That's a serious reason, and the text states it plainly. This is one of the heavy parts of the passage.

The answer is True. The text says, “So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.” (Leviticus 8:36) Moses, Israel's leader, gave the orders, and Aaron and his sons followed all of them. Seven days is a long time to stay put, so that's real obedience.
